nodes.label: Nine-stage study pipeline
nodes.rationale: Each stage names what it reads, what it writes, and what it will refuse to do, so a reader can tell a break from a change without running the code.

nodes.label: Stage 1 — ingest (immutable Stage 1 artifacts)
nodes.rationale: Do not re-run casually: re-running changes the vintage, and §12 forbids comparing numbers across vintages. --end is exclusive and clip_to_window() enforces it.

nodes.label: Stage 2 — segments and the window budget
nodes.rationale: The assertion is exact equality per origin, never against the pooled 4.9%: asserted pooled it fires spuriously at fourteen of fifteen origins, gets loosened until it passes, and then can no longer distinguish positional drift from ordinary between-origin variation.
nodes.norm_label: stage 2 — segments and the window budget

nodes.label: Stage 3 — the twelve per-bar variates
nodes.rationale: 75,091 usable bars produce 75,062 feature rows; the 29 dropped rows are one per segment because r is computed per segment. No variate uses a rolling window, which makes the center=True leak class unrepresentable.

nodes.label: Stage 3b — effective dimensionality and the gate
nodes.rationale: Gate PR at K=8 measures 4.393 < 5.0 so the gate does not pass; the prescribed action is disclosure, not a ladder re-cut, because D01 establishes there is no second consistent cut over F1-F5.
nodes.norm_label: stage 3b — effective dimensionality and the gate

nodes.label: Stage 4 — pre-flight invariants
nodes.rationale: Three checks, each of which failed the first time it ran: scale invariance MSE(c*x)/c^2 == MSE(x), single-batch overfit at dropout=0.0, and Naive-RW mapped as y_z = -mu_g/sigma_g.

nodes.label: Stage 5 — the pilot gate, judged on validation
nodes.rationale: Judged on the validation sub-block, never on test: §11 requires test blocks be opened once after the design is frozen, and a gate that repositions the title on a test-block result cannot coexist with that. Twelve cells are ordinary main-grid run_ids so Stage 6 skips them.
nodes.norm_label: stage 5 — the pilot gate, judged on validation

nodes.label: Stage 6 — the 534-run grid
nodes.rationale: 582 nominal cells minus 48 that are literally the same run: the horizon sweep's H=24 slice at seeds 42-44 shares run_ids with the main grid, and run_id is the identity of a run.

nodes.label: Stage 7 — evaluation of RQ1, RQ2, RQ3
nodes.rationale: Four things easy to get wrong are handled for the caller: order of operations on ratios, error bars bound to aggregation level, beta1's effective n, and a restricted studentized bootstrap.
nodes.norm_label: stage 7 — evaluation of rq1, rq2, rq3

nodes.label: Stage 8 — save paper_numbers.json
nodes.rationale: Every table and figure in the manuscript is generated from that file, never transcribed.

nodes.label: The notebook carries the package (twelve %%writefile cells)
nodes.rationale: A Kaggle session needs only the notebook and BTCUSDT_1h.parquet, so the repository is never uploaded. The notebook asserts the imported itransformer_btc lives in its own working directory, because two copies of the code with one stale is the failure the assertion exists to catch.
nodes.norm_label: the notebook carries the package (twelve %%writefile cells)

nodes.label: tools/build_notebook.py — notebook generator
nodes.rationale: Sits outside the package on purpose: it is build tooling, not study logic, and nothing under src/ may import it. Hand-editing a package cell in the notebook is a defect the next generator run reverts silently.

nodes.label: tests/test_notebook_sync.py — byte-identity assertion
nodes.rationale: Pays down the cost of a duplicated ~4,000-line copy: editing src/ without regenerating fails the suite.

nodes.label: Package module inventory and per-module guarantees
nodes.rationale: Each module is listed with the one guarantee it enforces, so a guarantee has a single owner: config derives the grid, splits raises on purge violation, model returns the target channel alone, runner shards the full manifest.
nodes.norm_label: package module inventory and per-module guarantees

nodes.label: run_id — deterministic run identity
nodes.rationale: {model}_o{origin:02d}_K{K:02d}_H{H:03d}_s{seed}. Changing any component deliberately orphans prior outputs rather than silently reusing a mismatched result.

nodes.label: artifacts/preds/{run_id}.parquet schema
nodes.rationale: timestamp is the window start, not the forecast origin. Since L=96 is a multiple of 24, hour-of-day is preserved, which is what makes the 00:00 UTC non-overlapping phase selectable by timestamp // 3.6e6 % 24 == 0.

nodes.label: artifacts/meta/{run_id}.json schema
nodes.rationale: Carries git_sha, code_sha256, input_parquet, input_sha256, input_sha256_source, mu_g, sigma_g, naive_rw_z and status, so every number resolves to a code identity and an input vintage.

nodes.label: code_sha256 — code identity where git is absent
nodes.rationale: git_sha is "unknown" on Kaggle because there is no git repository there, so the digest of the package source with line endings normalised is what identifies the code §12 requires every number to resolve to.
nodes.norm_label: code_sha256 — code identity where git is absent

nodes.label: input_sha256_source — report vs file-digest provenance
nodes.rationale: "report" when the digest came from the Stage 1 report beside the artifact, "file-digest" when the parquet was hashed directly; both are correct, and stating which is what makes the number checkable.

nodes.label: Two window semantics — contained vs origin
nodes.rationale: Train/validation use "contained" because the H-step target may not cross the boundary; test blocks use "origin" because §8.3 licenses the 96-bar lookback reaching back and blocking it would make evaluation unrealistically pessimistic. The two differ by exactly L+H-1 = 119 windows.
nodes.norm_label: two window semantics — contained vs origin

nodes.label: GPU-resident batching, no Dataset or DataLoader
nodes.rationale: At ~280k parameters the run is dominated by data movement and Python overhead, which a per-item loader maximises — roughly 10x worse, which puts the grid outside the 30 h weekly quota outright. nn.DataParallel is rejected because at batch 32 scatter/gather costs more than the split saves.
nodes.norm_label: gpu-resident batching, no dataset or dataloader

nodes.label: Two GPUs are two independent processes, not two threads
nodes.rationale: torch.manual_seed seeds every CUDA device, so two threads seeding concurrently would clobber each other's generator mid-run and §12's reproducibility contract would be unenforceable. One process per GPU with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES pinned gives each worker its own global RNG, interpreter lock and crash isolation.
nodes.norm_label: two gpus are two independent processes, not two threads

nodes.label: Four grid arms — main, uniform, fresh, horizon
nodes.rationale: main 300 (itr_), uniform 75 (itru_, attention forced uniform), fresh 15 (itrf_, one per origin at o_i+90d), horizon 144 (itr_, minus the 48 shared cells).
nodes.norm_label: four grid arms — main, uniform, fresh, horizon

nodes.label: Session budget guard checked at run boundaries
nodes.rationale: Bounds the session, not the worker: Kaggle's 12 h wall starts at cell 0, so the ~20-25 min prelude is subtracted before workers get their budget. Hitting the wall interactively loses /kaggle/working entirely, so the margin is not somewhere to be approximate.
nodes.norm_label: session budget guard checked at run boundaries

nodes.label: Evaluation cells gated on GRID_COMPLETE
nodes.rationale: A partial grid is an unbalanced panel and §9.1's estimators refuse one by design. Partial evaluation is never offered as a fallback, because a half-panel beta1 is a different estimand, not a noisier one.

nodes.label: Kaggle session chaining and glob-based resume
nodes.rationale: Roots are discovered by glob over /kaggle/input/*/preds and /kaggle/input/*/*/preds, never by dataset slug, so the Dataset's name and nesting do not matter. A run is complete only when both artifacts exist and meta.status == "complete".
nodes.norm_label: kaggle session chaining and glob-based resume

nodes.label: Column order is ladder order (K = first K columns)
nodes.rationale: Rung K is exactly the first K columns and r is channel 0 at every rung, so the target channel index never depends on the rung.
nodes.norm_label: column order is ladder order (k = first k columns)

nodes.label: Feature frame — 75,062 rows, 29 dropped one per segment
nodes.norm_label: feature frame — 75,062 rows, 29 dropped one per segment

nodes.label: Ratio metrics from seed-averaged MSEs, never averaged ratios
nodes.rationale: The two differ by Jensen, and the second would require pairing seed 42 at K=1 with seed 42 at K=8 — independent runs of different models where any of 5! orderings gives a different answer.
nodes.norm_label: ratio metrics from seed-averaged mses, never averaged ratios

nodes.label: Error bar bound to the aggregation level
nodes.rationale: Per-cell means mean ± std across seeds; anything aggregated across origins means SE across origins, with seed std reported separately as a Monte-Carlo diagnostic. Reporting seed std on an aggregated row understates headline uncertainty by roughly an order of magnitude.
nodes.norm_label: error bar bound to the aggregation level

nodes.label: beta1's effective n is the cluster count, bounded near 4
nodes.rationale: On a balanced panel with origin fixed effects beta1-hat reduces algebraically to the mean of the origin-specific within-slopes, so inference is a one-sample test on G = 15 numbers, and effective independence is bounded near 4 by the 79.2% training-window overlap between consecutive origins.
nodes.norm_label: beta1's effective n is the cluster count, bounded near 4

nodes.label: Restricted studentized one-sided wild cluster bootstrap, B = 99,999
nodes.rationale: Both Rademacher and Webb weights reported with the more conservative as the headline; the p-value floors at 1/(B+1) because no finite bootstrap supports a literal zero.
nodes.norm_label: restricted studentized one-sided wild cluster bootstrap, b = 99,999

nodes.label: Clark–West, not Diebold–Mariano, at the Stage 5 gate
nodes.rationale: K=1's feature set is a strict subset of K=8's under the same architecture and sample, so the pair is nested and standard DM is systematically undersized against exactly the alternative being tested.
nodes.norm_label: clark–west, not diebold–mariano, at the stage 5 gate

nodes.label: Expected numbers table — tell a break from a change
nodes.rationale: Pins 75,094 bars / 3 unusable, 75,062 feature rows, 15 origins, 70.12 MB largest tensor, 280,472 parameters, gate PR 4.393, and the first measured run's RelMSE 1.0183 / R2_oos -0.0183.
nodes.norm_label: expected numbers table — tell a break from a change

nodes.label: What is not built yet
nodes.rationale: Stated plainly because a reader should not have to discover it by running: comparison baselines (~255 runs), the economic evaluation, the optional K=16 rung, and a confirmed T4 timing. RQ1-RQ3 are answerable without the baselines because Naive-RW is computed from the scaler.

nodes.rationale: Committed so a Stage 2 run has something to be checked against rather than something to be tuned to; budget.py pins the values instead of recomputing them inside the test, because with both sides computed the same way a regression would agree with itself and pass.

nodes.label: Segment-wise window count Σ max(0, n_i − 119)
nodes.rationale: The assertion target, because it is the only form that is correct when a segment holds fewer than 120 bars.

nodes.label: The closed form is an upper bound, not an identity
nodes.source_location: What changed against the derived table
nodes.rationale: (bars − 119) − [119 × breaks + excluded] equals the segment-wise count only while every segment clears 120 bars. Origin 2022-02 contains an 80-bar segment: it contributes zero windows but the closed form charges it 80 − 119 = −39 and absorbs the negative silently. Seven origins are understated by 39 … 137 windows.

nodes.label: Raw-frame training range 13,558 … 15,217
nodes.rationale: A 10.9% spread, monotone in calendar time; largest training tensor 15,217 × 96 × 12 × 4 B = 70.12 MB.

nodes.label: Feature-frame training range 13,545 … 15,217
nodes.rationale: The tensors are cut from the feature frame, which holds one fewer bar per segment because r is computed per segment. The two frames are both right about different things, and the assertion target for a training run is the feature-frame count.

nodes.label: Subsampling floor is 13,545
nodes.rationale: Not 13,558 and emphatically not 13,520 — the control for the training-volume variation the fixed rolling window was chosen to eliminate.

nodes.label: Test blocks hold 720 forecast origins, not 601
nodes.rationale: Counting test blocks the training way returns 601 of 720 on a perfectly clean block — a 16.5% phantom loss that would read as outage damage and enter §9.2's block-coverage covariate as pure noise. The two semantics differ by exactly L + H − 1.
nodes.norm_label: test blocks hold 720 forecast origins, not 601

nodes.label: Exactly 3 unusable bars, the same 3 in all three senses
nodes.rationale: 2019-06-07T21:00, 2021-02-11T03:00, 2023-03-24T12:00. Total unusable is 3, not 9, which follows mechanically: no volume means no trades, and no trades means the bar's high and low never separate.
nodes.norm_label: exactly 3 unusable bars, the same 3 in all three senses

nodes.label: budget.py::COMMITTED_TRAIN_BUDGET pinned values
nodes.rationale: Regenerate the table and update the constant in the same commit, never one alone, or the assertion checks the artifact against a stale pin.

nodes.label: Gap blocks straddling a span boundary charged whole
nodes.source_location: What changed against the derived table
nodes.rationale: The derivation attributed a block to the span containing its gap_start; the measurement counts only positions actually inside the span. This moves counts in both directions, which is why some origins measured higher than derived and others lower.
nodes.norm_label: gap blocks straddling a span boundary charged whole

nodes.label: Test-window loss is conditioned on future gaps
nodes.rationale: Binance outages cluster on stress, so dropped targets are disproportionately high-volatility ones and survival depends on information unavailable at the forecast origin. A stated limitation, not a fixable defect.
nodes.norm_label: test-window loss is conditioned on future gaps

nodes.label: Training volume is not constant across origins
nodes.rationale: 13,558 … 15,217, monotone in calendar time and so correlated with the origin index and with everything compared across origins — partially reintroducing the variation the fixed rolling window was chosen to eliminate.
nodes.norm_label: training volume is not constant across origins

nodes.label: Regenerating the budget table
nodes.rationale: The table is a pure function of data/raw/BTCUSDT_1h.parquet and the constants, asserted by tests/test_data_plane.py.

nodes.rationale: Three of five adversarial lenses completed; consistency and Kaggle died on a session limit, and the verifier stage died too, so every entry was adjudicated by direct re-derivation against the document text or the artifact on disk. The pass is incomplete by construction, and saying otherwise would be the exact failure the register exists to prevent.
nodes.norm_label: second-pass audit provenance — two lenses never ran

nodes.label: Smaller corrections absorbed without a numbered entry
nodes.rationale: Each was verified and each changes one sentence, not a rule: the DM unit of observation, PT alignment with the trading rule, the seed-averaging order, the log-ratio demotion, the H==L measurement, §11 item 13 in window terms, and the hedged priority claim.
nodes.norm_label: smaller corrections absorbed without a numbered entry

nodes.label: Open items requiring external action
nodes.rationale: D16 citation verification blocks submission; D33 and D26 block Stage 2/Stage 4; the two unrun adversarial lenses block Stage 4 sign-off. D10 and D11 are struck through, closed by D33.

nodes.label: D01 — The K ladder does not add up
nodes.rationale: K=8 summed to nine and log_mean_trade_size was double-assigned. Given the family cardinalities the cut is forced, not chosen: only one assignment of the eight remaining variates satisfies both counts and keeps F2 intact as the redundancy control.
nodes.norm_label: d01 — the k ladder does not add up

nodes.label: D02 — The K_eff gate reads test-period data
nodes.rationale: A design decision informed by data the design is later evaluated on, with a qualitative trigger ("far below ~6.5") that admits any post-hoc reading. Fixed by the pre-first-origin span and a numeric trigger of PR < 5.0.
nodes.norm_label: d02 — the k_eff gate reads test-period data

nodes.label: D03 — The use_norm verification test cannot pass as written
nodes.rationale: The target is a channel of the same scaled array, so multiplying the input by c multiplies the target by c and the loss by c^2. A team running the source test would see it fail and either disable use_norm or chase a non-existent bug.
nodes.norm_label: d03 — the use_norm verification test cannot pass as written

nodes.label: D04 — Instance normalisation strips volatility level, confounding RQ1
nodes.rationale: The 8→12 rung can flatten because its information was normalised away — a mechanism entirely distinct from the redundancy the rung was designed to demonstrate. Any channel whose information content is its scale is reduced to its pattern.
nodes.norm_label: d04 — instance normalisation strips volatility level, confounding rq1

nodes.label: D05 — D(b) conflates model decay with market difficulty
nodes.rationale: A rising D(b) is consistent with model decay and with the market simply becoming harder, and the two are not separable; the source already defines RelMSE for period difficulty but never applies it to D(b). A(b) needs no correction because both models see the same block.
nodes.norm_label: d05 — d(b) conflates model decay with market difficulty

nodes.label: D06 — The decay regression is underspecified
nodes.rationale: Without origin fixed effects, between-origin baseline difficulty enters the residual and beta1 is identified partly from cross-origin differences rather than purely from time-since-training.
nodes.norm_label: d06 — the decay regression is underspecified

nodes.label: D07 — The origin count is credited to the wrong cause
nodes.rationale: The 2017-08 claim is false against the declared 2018-01-01 window, and a reader following it would fetch five extra months of data for no gain.
nodes.norm_label: d07 — the origin count is credited to the wrong cause

nodes.label: D08 — Horizon sweep K count stated two ways
nodes.rationale: 4 × 4 × 4 × 3 = 192 matches the stated total; 4 × 3 × 4 × 3 = 144 does not, so Stage 8 is the typo.
nodes.norm_label: d08 — horizon sweep k count stated two ways

nodes.label: D09 — Reference library says twelve origins
nodes.rationale: Stale text from the superseded futures-based design, superseded twice over.
nodes.norm_label: d09 — reference library says twelve origins

nodes.label: D10 — The artifact on disk violates the specification (ffill)
nodes.rationale: Alleged fill_policy=ffill with 122 synthetic bars would fabricate zero-return bars, force H=L=O=C and drive all three F2 estimators to zero immediately before whatever event caused the outage. Closed by D33: none of the three quoted keys exists on the artifact.
nodes.norm_label: d10 — the artifact on disk violates the specification (ffill)

nodes.label: D11 — The Stage 1 entry point is missing
nodes.rationale: Provenance must cite a tool that exists and a procedure that can be re-run. Closed by D33: the script exists at the repository root as spot_klines_btc.py.
nodes.norm_label: d11 — the stage 1 entry point is missing

nodes.label: D12 — signed_flow is a deterministic product of two other K=8 members
nodes.rationale: The product is nonlinear so it is not perfectly redundant, but the "maximum effective rank" claim is weaker than stated; kept because the interaction is the standard order-flow-imbalance construction, with the measured PR left to settle how much rank it contributes.
nodes.norm_label: d12 — signed_flow is a deterministic product of two other k=8 members

nodes.label: D13 — F2 estimators: per-bar or trailing-averaged
nodes.rationale: Per-bar with no trailing average: feeding a pre-smoothed estimator is strictly less informative, since the model can compute the average itself but cannot recover what smoothing destroyed. Consequence: no variate uses a rolling window at all, which licenses the no-embargo argument.
nodes.norm_label: d13 — f2 estimators: per-bar or trailing-averaged

nodes.label: D14 — Undefined denominators and a division by zero
nodes.rationale: A bar in which nothing traded carries no trade information, the same condition as downtime, so it takes the same policy — substituting any value would be imputation under another name. Side effect: log(volume), VWAP and the F2 logarithms become total functions.
nodes.norm_label: d14 — undefined denominators and a division by zero

nodes.label: D15 — Embargo declared justified with no justification
nodes.rationale: Silence on a López de Prado protocol element is exactly what a reviewer familiar with that literature will flag. The two-path argument is only airtight while every variate is a per-bar function.
nodes.norm_label: d15 — embargo declared justified with no justification

nodes.label: D16 — Unverified and mis-dated citations
nodes.rationale: The reference library states of itself that volumes, page ranges and DOIs were assembled from search results rather than published versions. Standing rule: no citation enters the manuscript without a verified DOI and the source read.

nodes.label: D17 — No control for "is a transformer needed at all?"
nodes.rationale: Ridge gives a clean two-way decomposition: ridge vs Naive-RW answers does the information help, iTransformer vs ridge answers does the architecture help, K=8 vs K=1 answers does cross-variate attention help. Without ridge the first two are entangled.
nodes.norm_label: d17 — no control for "is a transformer needed at all?"

nodes.label: D18 — Three seeds is too few for the headline claim
nodes.rationale: A standard deviation estimated from n=3 is itself extremely noisy, and reacting to seed noise after seeing results would be a design change made in response to the outcome.
nodes.norm_label: d18 — three seeds is too few for the headline claim

nodes.label: D19 — "Hours, not days" holds only in one implementation regime
nodes.rationale: The claim is not wrong, it is unconditioned, and the unstated condition is the difference between fitting the weekly quota and blowing through it.
nodes.norm_label: d19 — "hours, not days" holds only in one implementation regime

nodes.label: D20 — RelMSE near 1.00 is hard to read
nodes.rationale: R2_oos = 0.004 reads immediately; RelMSE = 0.996 does not. Anything above roughly 0.05 at this horizon should raise a leakage suspicion until re-verified.
nodes.norm_label: d20 — relmse near 1.00 is hard to read

nodes.label: D21 — Trading rule and directional accuracy undefined at H=24
nodes.rationale: The choice changes turnover by more than an order of magnitude and dominates every cost-adjusted number in Table 8. The cumulative forecast is what the position actually earns over the holding period; non-overlapping execution prevents the same forecast being traded 24 times.
nodes.norm_label: d21 — trading rule and directional accuracy undefined at h=24

nodes.label: D22 — No rung tests genuinely nonlinear features
nodes.rationale: An optional K=16 rung supplies a second high-nominal-K / low-K_eff control. It must be an explicit fifth rung; folded into the existing four it destroys the instrument.
nodes.norm_label: d22 — no rung tests genuinely nonlinear features

nodes.label: D23 — The pre-registered tau is arithmetically unreachable
nodes.rationale: Pure arithmetic on D20's own magnitudes: 1/0.996 − 1 = 0.402%, so all three thresholds demand the model become 2-10% worse than forecasting zero. RQ3 would return a null fixed before a single epoch runs, by a units mismatch rather than by the market.
nodes.norm_label: d23 — the pre-registered tau is arithmetically unreachable

nodes.label: D24 — No purge at the train/validation boundary
nodes.rationale: The contamination is small (~24 windows) but it lands on the split that decides early stopping and ridge alpha — the split that governs model selection. Validation-window inputs reaching back into training remain legitimate, so the input/target asymmetry is deliberate.
nodes.norm_label: d24 — no purge at the train/validation boundary

nodes.label: D25 — 17,400 is the 24-month count; training is 21 months
nodes.rationale: The coincidence with the tensor size (80.18 MB) and steps/epoch (545) is decisive: the numbers were derived from 24 months, not from the split. Either every downstream figure inherits a 14% error, or the implementation trains on all 24 months and validates in-sample, which is D24's leak.
nodes.norm_label: d25 — 17,400 is the 24-month count; training is 21 months

nodes.label: D26 — Block index b is collinear with calendar month
nodes.rationale: Settled by one expression: months visited for fixed b form a coset of <s> in Z12 of size 12/gcd(s,12). s=6 gives 2 months, s=3 gives 4, s=5 gives full decoupling. The entry first prescribed 3-month spacing and was corrected in place rather than silently rewritten — the register's own rule applies to the register.
nodes.norm_label: d26 — block index b is collinear with calendar month

nodes.label: D27 — The Stage 5 gate opens test blocks
nodes.rationale: Idempotence plus a deterministic run_id mean the resume logic finds the pilot runs complete and feeds them verbatim into Table 4 and the beta1 regression, so the origin that decided the framing re-enters the evidence for it. It is a selection event over the paper's conclusion, which the DSR does not correct.
nodes.norm_label: d27 — the stage 5 gate opens test blocks

nodes.label: D28 — Consecutive origins share most of their training data
nodes.rationale: Effective independence is bounded by total span / training window ≈ 4 regardless of spacing, so packing origins closer raises nominal G without adding information. At G=3 the disjoint-triple re-estimate will very likely be inconclusive, and that is itself the finding — it bounds what the full-panel p-value can honestly claim.
nodes.norm_label: d28 — consecutive origins share most of their training data

nodes.label: D29 — Every headline DM comparison is nested
nodes.rationale: Under nested models with estimated parameters the loss differential has a mean shifted away from zero and the statistic is not asymptotically N(0,1), so DM is undersized against exactly the alternative the paper wants to establish — and a viable paper can be killed by the wrong critical value at the Stage 5 gate.
nodes.norm_label: d29 — every headline dm comparison is nested

nodes.label: D30 — Seed std is the wrong error bar for origin-aggregated results
nodes.rationale: The two rules in §9.2 contradict each other: seeds are declared non-inferential for the regression and then made the sole uncertainty display for the results table, reintroducing exactly the overstated precision the wild cluster bootstrap was added to prevent.
nodes.norm_label: d30 — seed std is the wrong error bar for origin-aggregated results

nodes.label: D31 — y_z = 0 in scaler space is a drift forecast
nodes.rationale: mu_g varies by origin with the bull/bear cycle — the same cycle H2 invokes as its mechanism — so the nuisance is confounded with the effect of interest and does not wash out across origins.
nodes.norm_label: d31 — y_z = 0 in scaler space is a drift forecast

nodes.label: D32 — RQ1's K vs K_eff regression is not identified at three rung deltas
nodes.rationale: Adjacent deltas share an MSE with opposite sign (mechanical correlation ≈ −0.5) and three points plus an intercept leave 1 residual df, so the two specifications cannot be distinguished. The paper is titled after this comparison.
nodes.norm_label: d32 — rq1's k vs k_eff regression is not identified at three rung deltas

nodes.label: D33 — Empty data/raw and an out-of-window boundary bar
nodes.rationale: The audit's proposed fix — re-derive §4.1 from the report — is rejected because it would bake the out-of-window bar into the measured facts. The defect is in the artifact, not the table. Closes D10 and D11.
nodes.norm_label: d33 — empty data/raw and an out-of-window boundary bar

nodes.label: D34 — Newey–West Bartlett contradicts the dm.test validation target
nodes.rationale: Under the DM null h-step errors are MA(h−1), so all autocovariances to lag 23 are genuinely nonzero; Bartlett weights shrink gamma-hat_22 by ~92%, understating the long-run variance and producing the over-rejection the paragraph opens by warning against.
nodes.norm_label: d34 — newey–west bartlett contradicts the dm.test validation target

nodes.label: D35 — SPA and Reality Check cannot correct a pairwise matrix
nodes.rationale: The diagnosis is right and the remedy is the wrong tool: SPA's null is max_k E[d_k] <= 0 against one benchmark, not a family of pairwise nulls. With 8+ models the matrix holds 28+ tests, expecting ~1.4 spurious rejections under a complete null.
nodes.norm_label: d35 — spa and reality check cannot correct a pairwise matrix

nodes.label: D36 — Figure 3 plots A(b) for four K; A is one series
nodes.rationale: Left unfixed, whoever generates the figure invents a definition, and the figure and the regression then report different quantities under the same symbol — in the paper's graphical abstract. The per-origin-lines form also displays the actual identification.
nodes.norm_label: d36 — figure 3 plots a(b) for four k; a is one series

nodes.label: D37 — The linear-span argument is not a theorem under use_norm
nodes.rationale: Instance normalisation is itself a nonlinearity; d_model=128 > L=96 makes the projection generically injective; and the exclusion list is inconsistent with its own justification, since RSI and Bollinger bands are not linear in the lookback. The structural no-rolling-window consequence survives intact and rests on the twelve definitions, not on the span argument.
nodes.norm_label: d37 — the linear-span argument is not a theorem under use_norm

nodes.label: D38 — Validation-based hyperparameter selection that never occurs
nodes.rationale: Holding capacity fixed is what makes the rungs comparable, so no per-rung tuning is performed — but as written the flat 8→12 rung has an untested alternative explanation, which one robustness run at larger d_ff closes.
nodes.norm_label: d38 — validation-based hyperparameter selection that never occurs

nodes.label: D39 — Target-channel vs all-channel loss unspecified
nodes.rationale: Under an all-channel loss the amount of auxiliary supervision varies with the study's own independent variable, and K=1 is not the stated control but a different learning problem. The reference implementation defaults to the option that breaks the design.
nodes.norm_label: d39 — target-channel vs all-channel loss unspecified

nodes.label: D40 — Baselines carry no K assignment
nodes.rationale: The comparison an LTSF-literate reviewer cares about is iTransformer at K=8 versus PatchTST at K=8 on identical information. If PatchTST silently ran at K=1, the paper's central architectural comparison collapses into univariate-versus-multivariate.
nodes.norm_label: d40 — baselines carry no k assignment

nodes.label: D41 — b* has no estimator, origin index, or censoring method
nodes.rationale: min{.} does not commute with averaging, so pooled and per-origin b* are different estimands. The per-origin values are interval-censored survival data; a bare integer in the abstract violates the manuscript's own "never a bare number" rule.
nodes.norm_label: d41 — b* has no estimator, origin index, or censoring method

nodes.label: D42 — The wild cluster bootstrap recipe is incomplete
nodes.rationale: As written, two implementers get different p-values from identical prediction files — the exact failure §12's traceability contract exists to prevent. Every omitted choice (restricted vs unrestricted, studentized, B, alpha, sidedness, t(G−1)) moves the number.
nodes.norm_label: d42 — the wild cluster bootstrap recipe is incomplete

nodes.label: D43 — The leakage surface is declared closed on an incomplete enumeration
nodes.rationale: The no-rolling-window claim checks out; the closure claim built on it does not, because it is scoped to feature construction at the train-test boundary and fails at the first boundary that is not train-test. A closed-surface claim is also what stops the hunt §2 mandates.
nodes.norm_label: d43 — the leakage surface is declared closed on an incomplete enumeration

nodes.label: D44 — K_eff's span is undeclared and the statistic is blind to cross-lag structure
nodes.rationale: §11 item 5 audits only the gate, so a full-sample RQ1 regressor survives every existing checklist item by construction. And two variates can be near-uncorrelated contemporaneously yet near-redundant to a model with a 96-hour lookback — a measurement-validity failure rather than a finding if unaddressed.
nodes.norm_label: d44 — k_eff's span is undeclared and the statistic is blind to cross-lag structure

nodes.label: D45 — Window loss is reported globally; per-block it reaches 50%
nodes.rationale: An assertion against a 4.9% global estimate fires spuriously at most origins and would predictably be loosened until it passes — disarming the single defence against the pipeline's most likely silent failure. §4.3 names the bug the assertion exists to catch; specified at the wrong granularity it cannot catch it.
nodes.norm_label: d45 — window loss is reported globally; per-block it reaches 50%

nodes.label: D46 — Unfixed trade phase, gap-spanning returns, unimplementable DSR
nodes.rationale: With N=621 and T=180 the DSR threshold is essentially unmeetable — a second guaranteed null alongside D23, reading to a referee as either a failed strategy or a misapplied statistic with no way to tell which. §13.5 is also the one place returns are computed outside the segment-aware feature code.
nodes.norm_label: d46 — unfixed trade phase, gap-spanning returns, unimplementable dsr

nodes.label: D47 — The LR schedule makes the epoch budget decorative
nodes.rationale: Training adequacy is otherwise an alternative explanation for every K contrast: a K=12 model has 12 tokens of attention structure to fit in the same ~7 effective epochs as a K=1 model with none.
nodes.norm_label: d47 — the lr schedule makes the epoch budget decorative

nodes.label: D48 — Four outcome-determining choices left open after results
nodes.rationale: A document otherwise scrupulous about pre-registration leaves four levers unfixed — and the pre-registered thresholds are precisely the ones that cost nothing, while slippage, which decides whether the strategy makes money, is blank.
nodes.norm_label: d48 — four outcome-determining choices left open after results

nodes.label: D49 — The flat 8→12 rung has the fewest seeds and no equivalence test
nodes.rationale: "Flat 8→12" is an assertion of no effect, and a non-significant delta is a failure to reject rather than evidence of equivalence — at n=3 a near-guaranteed failure to reject regardless of the truth. The paper would assert the designed contrast without being able to show it.
nodes.norm_label: d49 — the flat 8→12 rung has the fewest seeds and no equivalence test

nodes.label: D50 — The uniform-attention control is never used as an arm
nodes.rationale: K=1 versus K=8 varies information and architecture simultaneously, so a decaying A(b) is equally consistent with a capacity story as with the information story RQ2 claims. Ridge separates them only under a linear model; uniform attention is the only control that does it within the architecture under study.
nodes.norm_label: d50 — the uniform-attention control is never used as an arm

nodes.label: D54 — The launcher cannot run without a second Dataset
nodes.rationale: Three defects with one root cause: the launcher assumed the repository would be present on the machine that runs it, so §12's traceability contract lost both its code half (git_sha unknown) and its input half (hard-coded report path) at precisely the place the grid executes. Files rather than in-cell definitions, because the grid runs as subprocesses that inherit none of the kernel's namespace.
nodes.norm_label: d54 — the launcher cannot run without a second dataset

nodes.label: D54e — Partial sessions crashed the evaluation cells
nodes.rationale: The estimators are right to refuse an unbalanced panel; where the exception landed was not — the last cells of a twelve-hour session, marking the Kaggle version failed at the moment its output was the only thing worth keeping.
nodes.norm_label: d54e — partial sessions crashed the evaluation cells

nodes.label: D54f — The budget clock started inside each worker
nodes.rationale: Kaggle's 12 h wall runs from the notebook's first cell, so the ~20-25 min prelude sat outside the budget and the two clocks drifted. Hitting the wall interactively loses /kaggle/working entirely, so the margin is not somewhere to be approximate.
nodes.norm_label: d54f — the budget clock started inside each worker

nodes.label: Research Specification: Nominal Variates vs Effective Dimensionality in iTransformer
nodes.rationale: Spot-only, single-asset, feature-based revision. Multi-asset spot (12 crypto log-returns) rejected by user decision; futures-based features rejected by the spot-only constraint. Title is locked only after experiments conclude.
nodes.norm_label: research specification: nominal variates vs effective dimensionality in itransformer

nodes.label: RQ1 — Nominal count K or effective dimensionality K_eff?
nodes.rationale: H1: benefit tracks K_eff, with real gains at K=1→4→8 and flat 8→12. Reframed from 'does K help' to 'does K or K_eff govern the benefit'. The distinction is one the iTransformer paper does not draw, and its own benchmark heterogeneity (7 features vs 321 clients) invites it.
nodes.norm_label: rq1 — nominal count k or effective dimensionality k_eff?

nodes.label: RQ2 — Does the multivariate-over-univariate gap narrow with time-since-training?
nodes.rationale: H2: it narrows, because the microstructure-to-return mapping is regime-specific. Compares K=1 against K=8, never K=12: K=8 is the rung of maximum effective rank, so using K=12 would confound decay with the redundancy deliberately built into that rung.
nodes.norm_label: rq2 — does the multivariate-over-univariate gap narrow with time-since-training?

nodes.label: RQ3 — Optimal retraining cadence, and does it depend on K?
nodes.rationale: H3: larger K decays faster. b* = min{b : D(b) > tau}. Without a fixed rule 'optimal cadence' is describable but not answerable.
nodes.norm_label: rq3 — optimal retraining cadence, and does it depend on k?

nodes.label: Pre-registered degradation threshold tau
nodes.rationale: Headline tau = 5%, sensitivity at {2.5%, 5%, 10%}. Choosing the threshold after seeing the decay curve is indistinguishable from p-hacking.

nodes.label: K_eff — effective dimensionality
nodes.rationale: The whole point of the family grouping is that nominal count and effective rank diverge, and that divergence is the object of RQ1.

nodes.label: The K ladder (1 / 4 / 8 / 12)
nodes.rationale: Expected K_eff 1 / ~3.5 / ~6.5 / ~7. Those values are reasoned from family structure, not measured; if measured PR at K=8 lands near 4 the ladder must be re-cut before the main grid. Fix the hypothesis to the measurement, never the reverse.

nodes.label: K=12 rung as deliberate redundancy control
nodes.rationale: Adds four nominal variates carrying almost no additional rank. A flat 8→12 rung is not a failed experiment but the demonstration that nominal K is the wrong axis. Must be stated explicitly in the methodology or a reviewer reads it as a null result.
nodes.norm_label: k=12 rung as deliberate redundancy control

nodes.label: K=1 attention degeneracy as the designed control
nodes.rationale: At N=1 softmax over a single token gives weight 1, so attention is an identity and the model reduces to Linear(L→d_model) → LayerNorm → FFN → Linear(d_model→H). Every other component is identical, so the K=1 arm isolates the contribution of cross-variate attention. Left unexplained an examiner reads it as an implementation error.
nodes.norm_label: k=1 attention degeneracy as the designed control

nodes.label: Participation ratio PR = (sum lambda)^2 / sum lambda^2
nodes.rationale: Computed on the correlation matrix of each K rung; bounded between 1 and K. Supplies K_eff as RQ1's independent variable.
nodes.norm_label: participation ratio pr = (sum lambda)^2 / sum lambda^2

nodes.label: Rolling participation ratio (90-day window)
nodes.rationale: Tests whether the dependency structure is stable across 2018–2026. The swing matters more than the level.

nodes.label: Rolling OLS R² of r_{t+1} on K=8 features
nodes.rationale: If R²(t) is unstable, H2's premise is established before a single epoch runs. It is also the early warning for the flat-4→8 risk: if microstructure R² is already near zero and stable, renegotiate the title at Stage 3b rather than after the main grid.
nodes.norm_label: rolling ols r2 of r_{t+1} on k=8 features

nodes.label: Shifting participant-composition mechanism behind H2
nodes.rationale: Replaces the unavailable cross-asset correlation-instability mechanism of the multi-asset design. Retail flow 2018–2020, the 2021 leverage cycle, institutional flow after 2024 spot ETF approval; order-flow predictability should decay as market making tightens. Rests on one finance-theoretic and one ML-theoretic foundation independently.

nodes.label: BTCUSDT spot 1h dataset, 2018-01-01 → 2026-08-01
nodes.rationale: ~75,216 bars, end exclusive, UTC throughout.

nodes.label: Binance REST /api/v3/klines
nodes.rationale: The REST API is now sufficient, reversing the earlier bulk-archive decision: bulk was required only for openInterestHist, topLongShortAccountRatio and takerlongshortRatio, which serve 30 days over the API. ~76 paginated requests cover eight years at ~380 weight against a 6,000/min ceiling.

nodes.label: binance_spot_klines.py (Stage 1 ingest)
nodes.rationale: Outputs BTCUSDT_1h.parquet + _report.json + _gaps.csv.

nodes.label: Spot-only constraint (no futures data)
nodes.rationale: funding_rate, oi_change, ls_account_ratio and basis are removed. Costs four variates, buys longer history (spot reaches 2017-08 vs futures 2019-09, spanning the 2018 bear market and the COVID crash), one provenance justification rather than three, and eliminates the multi-symbol availability probe.

nodes.label: Retention of all eleven meaningful kline columns
nodes.rationale: A fetcher truncating to OHLCV silently destroys F3, F4 and F5, collapsing the ladder from 12 to 6. quote_asset_volume feeds VWAP, number_of_trades feeds intensity, taker_buy_base_volume feeds signed flow. The twelfth field `ignore` is dropped. Numeric fields arrive as strings and without explicit coercion every downstream computation is silently wrong rather than raising.
nodes.norm_label: retention of all eleven meaningful kline columns

nodes.label: Segmentation, never imputation
nodes.rationale: Gaps split the series into contiguous segments; windows are built inside segments, never across them. No reindexing to a full grid, no filling. Log-returns are computed per segment (first bar NaN, dropped) before the scaler is fitted, otherwise cross-gap returns contaminate mu_g and sigma_g.

nodes.label: Rubin's MCAR/MAR/MNAR taxonomy does not apply to exchange downtime
nodes.rationale: BTCUSDT has traded every second for eight years, so zero-trade intervals are ruled out and only downtime remains. When the exchange is down no price forms, so imputation is not risky but undefined — there is no ground truth, therefore no metric can justify any imputation choice. This also retires the MNAR diagnostic.
nodes.norm_label: rubin's mcar/mar/mnar taxonomy does not apply to exchange downtime

nodes.label: Why forward-fill (and interpolation) is actively wrong here
nodes.rationale: ffill manufactures a zero-then-jump pattern that never occurred and a model will learn it. It forces H=L=O=C so Parkinson and Garman–Klass return zero volatility immediately before an extreme bar, poisoning F2; volume=0 gives log(0)=-inf and taker_buy_ratio=0/0 gives NaN. Linear interpolation removes the zero-then-jump but understates realized volatility at outage boundaries — opposite bias, equal contamination.
nodes.norm_label: why forward-fill (and interpolation) is actively wrong here

nodes.label: gap_blocks — the number to read from the fetcher report
nodes.rationale: Cost is dominated by block count, not gap length: forty one-hour gaps cost ~4,800 windows, one forty-hour gap ~159. Below ~100 blocks losses stay under 16% of ~75,000 windows.
nodes.norm_label: gap_blocks — the number to read from the fetcher report

nodes.label: Window-loss cost accounting: 119 × gap_blocks + missing bars
nodes.rationale: A gap of g bars invalidates L+H-1+g start positions; at L=96, H=24 that is 119+g. The rejected-window count is logged per origin and asserted against this estimate — a mismatch means timestamps and the data array have drifted out of alignment.
nodes.norm_label: window-loss cost accounting: 119 × gap_blocks + missing bars

nodes.label: Validate windows by timestamp, not by positional index
nodes.rationale: Named the highest-probability silent bug in the whole pipeline: if windows are slid over a positional index after dropna(), gaps close silently and windows cross time discontinuities without raising anything.
nodes.norm_label: validate windows by timestamp, not by positional index

nodes.label: Rejection of the 'near-gap' indicator variate
nodes.rationale: A binary flag marking bars adjacent to an outage would make gap-spanning windows usable but belongs to none of F1–F5, breaking the ladder and rendering the K=8 vs K=12 contrast uninterpretable. Losing a few percent of windows is far cheaper than contaminating the study's primary independent variable.

nodes.label: No winsorization, no outlier removal
nodes.rationale: Clipping at ±5σ removes exactly the events driving regime-dependent decay. Extreme regimes are the object of study, not noise. State the decision explicitly or a reviewer reads it as an oversight.

nodes.label: Backward-looking rolling windows only (center=False)
nodes.rationale: Every rolling indicator must use pandas.rolling(center=False); center=True is a fatal leak.

nodes.label: F1 — Price trajectory (r, upper_shadow, lower_shadow)
nodes.rationale: 3 independent degrees of freedom.

nodes.label: F2 — Volatility estimators (Parkinson, Garman–Klass, Rogers–Satchell)
nodes.rationale: ~1 dof, redundant by construction — which is why they form the deliberately redundant 8→12 rung.

nodes.label: F3 — Intensity (log_quote_volume, log_trade_count, log_mean_trade_size)
nodes.rationale: 2 dof: the third is the difference of the first two.

nodes.label: F4 — Order flow (taker_buy_ratio, signed_flow)
nodes.rationale: 1–2 dof; carries direction, not magnitude.

nodes.label: F5 — Intrabar price location ((VWAP − C)/(H − L))
nodes.rationale: 1 dof; VWAP = quote_volume / volume.
nodes.norm_label: f5 — intrabar price location ((vwap − c)/(h − l))

nodes.label: Exclusion of log(C/O) as a separate variate
nodes.rationale: Crypto bars are contiguous so log(C/O) ≈ r at correlation ≈ 0.99. It appeared in the earlier K=5 layer as oc_return and is removed: silent duplication inflates K without inflating K_eff, corrupting the very axis RQ1 measures.
nodes.norm_label: exclusion of log(c/o) as a separate variate

nodes.label: Target: log_return, single- and multi-step
nodes.rationale: Forecasting price levels produces artificially low MSE because price is near a random walk and a persistence baseline matches any model. The log-return transform — not the scaler — is what stabilizes the series; the residual heteroskedasticity is handled by instance normalization inside iTransformer.

nodes.label: StandardScaler fitted on the training window only
nodes.rationale: Three reasons for the paper: literature comparability (all LTSF results are on z-scored data), inertness under use_norm=True, and consistency across models including baselines lacking internal normalization. Refit at every origin on the 21-month training sub-block, never on validation or test.
nodes.norm_label: standardscaler fitted on the training window only

nodes.label: Algebraic cancellation of the outer affine scaler under instance norm
nodes.rationale: With z=(x−mu_g)/sigma_g, instance stats m and s carry the same factors, so (z−m)/s = (x−mean_t(x_W))/std_t(x_W) and mu_g, sigma_g vanish. True for StandardScaler, RobustScaler and MinMaxScaler alike, so the scaler choice cannot affect what iTransformer learns. What it does control is the reporting scale (MSE in units of sigma_g²) and learning for LSTM/ARIMA which lack internal normalization.
nodes.norm_label: algebraic cancellation of the outer affine scaler under instance norm

nodes.label: Why the fat-tail argument does not favour RobustScaler
nodes.rationale: On fat tails sigma > IQR/1.349, so dividing by the smaller quantity makes outliers larger in scaled space and lets crash bars dominate MSE more — exactly wrong for a study about regime behaviour. The fat-tail concern argues for Huber or MAE loss, not a different scaler. A one-origin three-seed robustness check is expected to show the RelMSE difference inside seed variance.
nodes.norm_label: why the fat-tail argument does not favour robustscaler

nodes.label: MinMaxScaler excluded on correctness grounds
nodes.rationale: Bounded by training min/max, it emits out-of-[0,1] values whenever a test regime exceeds the training range. A recurring defect in the crypto LSTM literature, where it is applied to price levels so every new all-time high falls outside the fitted range — worth one sentence in Related Work.

nodes.label: use_norm=True — instance normalization, mandatory not a tuning knob
nodes.rationale: Each input window is normalized by its own statistics along the time dimension and denormalized at output. It has architectural consequences that determine how the preprocessing scaler must be justified; if disabled, the entire scaler analysis collapses.
nodes.norm_label: use_norm=true — instance normalization, mandatory not a tuning knob

nodes.label: use_norm scale-invariance verification test
nodes.rationale: Train one model on StandardScaler output and one on the same input × 100; under use_norm=True both losses must be identical to numerical precision. Run before anything else at Stage 5.

nodes.label: iTransformer encoder-only architecture
nodes.rationale: (B,L,N) → transpose → InvertedEmbedding Linear(L→d_model) → e_layers of MHA over N tokens / LayerNorm / FFN / LayerNorm → Projection Linear(d_model→H) → select target channel.

nodes.label: Cross-variate attention (each variate is a token)
nodes.rationale: Attention operates across variates rather than across time steps, which is why its attention sequence length equals N, not L.
nodes.norm_label: cross-variate attention (each variate is a token)

nodes.label: Hyperparameter configuration (L=96, H=24, d_model=128, d_ff=256, e_layers=2, n_heads=8)
nodes.rationale: d_model reduced from 512 to 128 because iTransformer's attention sequence length equals N (at most 12), not L; d_model=512 over-parameterizes against ~17,000 training samples. Adam at 1e-4 with type-1 schedule, batch 32, 30 epochs, patience 5 on validation MSE, seeds 42/43/44.
nodes.norm_label: hyperparameter configuration (l=96, h=24, d_model=128, d_ff=256, e_layers=2, n_heads=8)

nodes.label: Naive-RW baseline (ŷ = 0 for log-return)
nodes.rationale: Mandatory EMH baseline. A random walk in price implies zero expected return; using the last return produces a weaker baseline and makes results look better than they are.

nodes.label: ARIMA baseline (order by AIC on the training window)
nodes.norm_label: arima baseline (order by aic on the training window)

nodes.label: DLinear baseline (trend-seasonal decomposition + linear)
nodes.rationale: Not optional — a missing DLinear is the first thing a reviewer familiar with the LTSF literature will flag.

nodes.label: PatchTST baseline (patch 16, stride 8, channel-independent)
nodes.rationale: SOTA channel-independent transformer; if RQ1 returns null the paper repositions as a finding supporting PatchTST's channel-independence claim.

nodes.label: Rolling-origin walk-forward validation with purging
nodes.rationale: 24-month fixed training window (21-month train sub-block + final 3 months validation), H-step purge at the train–test boundary, embargo not applied, 6 × 30-day test blocks with no retraining, 6-month origin spacing. Rolling rather than expanding because with an expanding window the training set size changes at each origin, so model age cannot be separated from training data volume.

nodes.label: H-step purge at every train–test boundary
nodes.rationale: The `- H` term in window enumeration is the purge: the last retained training window's target ends exactly at T_end, so no observation is discarded — only ~24 window configurations out of ~17,400. It shares its logic with segmentation: neither discards observations, both discard window configurations.
nodes.norm_label: h-step purge at every train–test boundary

nodes.label: Origin derivation — 13 origins, 2020-01 … 2026-01
nodes.rationale: Each origin consumes 24 months training + 180 days test = 30 months. With the 2018-01→2026-08 window at 6-month spacing that yields thirteen; the final origin tests through 2026-06-30. Spot history starting 2017-08 is what makes thirteen possible; the futures-based design reached only ten.

nodes.label: build_windows() — timestamp-validated window builder
nodes.rationale: The `continue` branch is the only thing standing between the pipeline and a silent cross-gap window.

nodes.label: Rejection of Combinatorial Purged Cross-Validation
nodes.rationale: CPCV generates backtest paths with non-chronological block ordering, under which time-since-training — RQ2's primary independent variable — is undefined. CPCV also assumes stability of the data-generating process across blocks, which this study explicitly tests. Paragraph included verbatim in the methodology.

nodes.label: Experiment grid (~517 runs)
nodes.rationale: Main grid 13 × 4K × 3 seeds = 156; horizon sweep 4 × 4 × 4 × 3 = 192; baselines 13 × (4 deterministic + 3 stochastic × 3) = 169. Up from 430 because the ladder grew from three rungs to four; K=12's runs cannot be trimmed without removing the control.

nodes.label: RelMSE = MSE_model(b) / MSE_naive(b)
nodes.rationale: Controls for period difficulty; being a ratio, the scaler's scale factor cancels.

nodes.label: A(b) = [MSE_K1(b) − MSE_K8(b)] / MSE_K1(b) — RQ2 dependent variable
nodes.rationale: A ratio of MSEs and right-skewed, so log(MSE_K1/MSE_K8) is better behaved under OLS and reduces to A(b) for small differences; report both and note the choice.
nodes.norm_label: a(b) = [mse_k1(b) − mse_k8(b)] / mse_k1(b) — rq2 dependent variable

nodes.label: D(b) = [MSE(b) − MSE(1)] / MSE(1) — RQ3 degradation curve
nodes.norm_label: d(b) = [mse(b) − mse(1)] / mse(1) — rq3 degradation curve

nodes.label: ΔMSE per rung — RQ1 dependent variable
nodes.rationale: Regressed separately on K and on K_eff.
nodes.norm_label: δmse per rung — rq1 dependent variable

nodes.label: MAPE prohibited on log-returns
nodes.rationale: Log-returns frequently approach zero so the denominator explodes. On reconstructed prices it is dominated by random-walk behaviour and uninformative. The Lewis (1982) thresholds commonly cited in Indonesian journals do not apply.

nodes.label: Diebold–Mariano test for every comparative claim
nodes.rationale: Validate any custom Python implementation against R's forecast::dm.test().
nodes.norm_label: diebold–mariano test for every comparative claim

nodes.label: HAC (Newey–West) variance estimator at lag h−1
nodes.rationale: Required at H>1 because forecast errors overlap; at H=24 that means lag 23. Skipping the correction produces over-optimistic p-values.
nodes.norm_label: hac (newey–west) variance estimator at lag h−1

nodes.label: Harvey–Leybourne–Newbold small-sample correction
nodes.rationale: S* = S·sqrt[(T+1−2h+h(h−1)/T)/T], compared against Student-t with T−1 df, not the standard normal.

nodes.label: Decay regression A(b) = β₀ + β₁·b + ε — the paper's core claim
nodes.rationale: A significant β₁ < 0 is the affirmative answer to the title question. The naive OLS specification is wrong: 13 origins × 6 blocks = 78 observations, but blocks within an origin come from the same trained model so residuals correlate within origin. Cluster by origin; average over seeds first (seeds are computational noise, not population draws — treating them as 234 observations is not defensible); a random-intercept mixed model is an acceptable alternative.
nodes.norm_label: decay regression a(b) = β0 + β1·b + ε — the paper's core claim

nodes.label: Wild cluster bootstrap at 13 clusters
nodes.rationale: With only 13 clusters — well under the usual 30–40 rule of thumb — conventional cluster-robust standard errors are biased downward. Python `wildboottest`, R `fwildclusterboot`. Listed under risk as 'certain': not a risk to mitigate but a specification to get right.

nodes.label: Preliminary market-efficiency tests (Variance Ratio, Hurst, ADF)
nodes.rationale: arch.unitroot.VarianceRatio, an R/S Hurst implementation, and statsmodels adfuller. This is what converts 'efficient market' from an assumption into a finding.
nodes.norm_label: preliminary market-efficiency tests (variance ratio, hurst, adf)

nodes.label: Eleven-stage execution pipeline
nodes.rationale: Ingest → data validation → feature construction → pre-model measurement → split generator → RQ1 pilot → main grid → baselines → horizon sweep → aggregation and testing → attention extraction → economic evaluation.

nodes.label: Stage 3b gate — re-cut the ladder if measured K_eff at K=8 is far below ~6.5
nodes.rationale: Rated medium–high likelihood and detected before any training, which is why Stage 3b precedes Stage 5.
nodes.norm_label: stage 3b gate — re-cut the ladder if measured k_eff at k=8 is far below ~6.5

nodes.label: Stage 5 RQ1 pilot — decision gate on K=1 vs K=8
nodes.rationale: 1 origin × 4 K × 3 seeds. The gate is K=1 vs K=8, never K=1 vs K=12: K=12 is built to be redundant and gating on it would kill a viable paper for the wrong reason. If K=8 does not significantly beat K=1, reposition the title to the descriptive variant now, not in week nine.
nodes.norm_label: stage 5 rq1 pilot — decision gate on k=1 vs k=8

nodes.label: Persist raw predictions, not just metrics
nodes.rationale: Required for the DM test, per-regime analysis and economic evaluation. Re-running 430 experiments because predictions were not saved is an expensive mistake.
nodes.norm_label: persist raw predictions, not just metrics

nodes.label: Stage 10 — cross-variate attention extraction and regime heatmaps
nodes.rationale: Attention weights per block, heatmaps for calm versus stress regime → Figure 5.
nodes.norm_label: stage 10 — cross-variate attention extraction and regime heatmaps

nodes.label: Stage 11 — economic evaluation with transaction costs
nodes.rationale: Long/short rule from directional predictions, 0.04% taker fee + slippage; Sharpe, max drawdown, turnover before and after costs.
nodes.norm_label: stage 11 — economic evaluation with transaction costs

nodes.label: IMRaD paper structure, 10–14 pages
nodes.rationale: Abstract 200–250 words must contain concrete numbers — β₁, percentage decay, recommended cadence — because an abstract without numbers reads like a proposal, not a result. Section 4.3 (RQ2 decay) is the core of the paper.

nodes.label: Figure 3 — decay curve A(b) versus b
nodes.rationale: Carries the entire paper; if only one figure could appear in a graphical abstract it is Figure 3.
nodes.norm_label: figure 3 — decay curve a(b) versus b

nodes.label: Table 2b — eigenvalue spectrum and participation ratio per K rung
nodes.rationale: Changed role: it previously argued K=12 is not redundant, and now measures how redundant each rung is — that measurement is RQ1's independent variable rather than a defensive footnote.
nodes.norm_label: table 2b — eigenvalue spectrum and participation ratio per k rung

nodes.label: Leakage checklist (first five items fatal)
nodes.rationale: Three bolded items (timestamp validation, per-segment returns, no reindexing) replace the former 'forward-fill only, never bfill' rule: that rule prevents lookahead correctly but does not make ffill safe when the target is a log-return.

nodes.label: Risk register and title-repositioning contingency
nodes.rationale: If RQ1 is null, switch the title to 'Effective Dimensionality and Temporal Decay in Cross-Variate Attention'. No detectable decay is still a valid finding (the advantage is structural, not regime-specific). If seed variance exceeds the effect, increase to 5 seeds. If GPU quota is exhausted, trim the horizon sweep to 2 origins.
